$comment: The registry of controls this repository claims to have, and the probe that proves each claim.
version: a document may not assert that a control is configured unless a probe named here
reads that configuration from its own source of truth. Prose is a claim; a probe is evidence.
JSON rather than YAML on purpose. This repo has no YAML parser dependency, so a YAML
registry would need a hand-written one — and a hand-written parser that silently matches
nothing is exactly the failure this registry exists to catch. A registry whose own reader
could quietly return an empty set would be the joke writing itself.
src/tests/unit/control-registry.test.ts enforces the invariants: every probe path exists and
is wired into the workflow named here, every adr path exists, nothing may claim
status 'configured' without a scheduled probe, and every control-shaped ADR has an entry.

controls.claims: main requires both CI check runs to pass before a pull request can merge
controls.knownLimit: The probe reports; it cannot enable protection, and it deliberately still exits 0 on an honestly-documented absence — failing a scheduled audit over a console action nobody in CI can perform would make the audit a permanent red that people learn to ignore. What changed is that the finding now reaches a person: the audit opens and updates one merge-gate-unenforced issue when the acceptance goes stale, or when ADR 015's own precondition is met. Until 2026-08-31 this probe's finding went into a log file and stopped, which made it the only control here whose result nothing carried.
controls.humanAction: GitHub → Settings → Branches → add a rule for main. Required contexts are the exact strings in requiredContexts; run `pnpm exec vitest run required-checks-contract` first, which proves they are the strings GitHub publishes today. Never type `verify` or `e2e` — those are job IDs and would register two contexts nothing reports, blocking every PR permanently.
controls.acceptedWhy: Restated 2026-09-15 by the defects review, and still a deliberate choice. The original acceptance stands on its own terms: the 2026-08-29 blackout is what this gap costs when it is called — eleven consecutive CI runs on main died at Install dependencies, every check after reported skipped, and eleven pull requests were merged by hand against a gate that had not run. ADR 015 said protection was only reasonable once a passing run existed to enforce against; that blocker is gone. It stays accepted only because enabling protection is a GitHub console action nobody in CI can perform, and probe-branch-protection.mjs escalates it under the merge-gate-unenforced label rather than letting it go quiet. What changed today is where the staleness of this line is enforced: it was asserted inside the merge gate itself, so on 2026-10-01 it would have turned every pull request red over a console action no diff can affect — the same severity misplacement ADR 029 records. The age check now runs in control-audit.yml and opens an issue; the gate keeps only the structural assertions a diff can actually break.

controls.claims: the five production-smoke secrets are scoped to the production-readonly environment, not to the repository
controls.humanAction: GitHub → Settings → Environments → production-readonly: put the five secrets there and set the variable SMOKE_SECRETS_SOURCE=environment. Never set that marker at repository scope — it is what distinguishes isolated from merely green.
controls.knownLimit: A convention, not an enforcement. GitHub gives a job no way to ask where a secret came from, so setting the marker at repository scope defeats it. Recorded rather than overclaimed — ADR 006.
controls.acceptedWhy: Restated 2026-09-15 by the defects review, and corrected: the previous reason named the wrong blocker. Issue #24 is that SHOPIFY_ADMIN_ACCESS_TOKEN holds a token of the wrong kind, which is a different fact from this control, and citing it here made an unmet isolation requirement read as a downstream consequence of a credential problem. This control is about scope, not validity: the five smoke secrets must sit on the production-readonly GitHub Environment with the SMOKE_SECRETS_SOURCE=environment marker, because this repository is public and forkable and repository-scoped secrets are readable by every workflow. Correcting the token would not close this gap; moving the secrets would, whatever the token holds. It stays accepted because both are GitHub console actions nobody in CI can perform, and preflight-secrets.mjs asserts the marker so the difference between isolated and merely green stays observable.

controls.claims: something asks, every six hours, whether healthyjewellery.com and its www host both reach this project's production deployment on the same commit — and reports the answer whatever it is
controls.knownLimit: Two limits, both deliberate. First, nothing watches control-audit.yml, so if that workflow stops executing this check goes silent and its silence is indistinguishable from an all-clear — the same shape control-acceptance-freshness records one tier up, and the weekly human backstop is what covers it. Second, this entry claims that something *asks*, not that the domain is currently bound: the live verdict is the probe's output, in canonical-domain.json and in one domain-unbound issue, and is deliberately not copied into this file. A hand-edited registry holding a live fact is a second copy that drifts from the first, which is the shape ADR 018 exists to refuse.
controls.humanAction: None while this reads green. When it opens a domain-unbound issue, the action is in Vercel -> Project -> Settings -> Domains: both hostnames attached to this project and assigned to Production, with www permanently redirecting to the apex. Never change DNS at Shopify — docs/dns-domain-setup.md records why a ssl.com CAA record would block Vercel's own certificate renewal.

controls.claims: every deliberately-accepted control gap is re-decided within 30 days, and a person is told when one is not
controls.knownLimit: Nothing watches this probe. probe-ci-liveness.mjs watches ci.yml and probe-smoke-liveness.mjs watches production-smoke.yml, but no probe watches control-audit.yml — so if that workflow stops executing, this check goes silent and its silence is indistinguishable from an all-clear. That is the exact shape ADR 022 names, one tier up, and it is stated here rather than implied because an unstated limit is how the merge gate stayed dark for eleven runs. The weekly human backstop is what covers it today.
controls.humanAction: None while this reads green. When it opens a control-acceptance-stale issue, the action is to re-decide the named gap in docs/controls.json — either close it, or update acceptedSince and acceptedWhy to say it is still a deliberate choice. Never bump the date without re-reading the reason: that is the snooze this control exists to make visible.

controls.claims: every workflow runs its steps under pipefail, so a piped step cannot report success for a failing command
the 80% coverage thresholds in vitest.config.ts are evaluated by the merge gate and applied to every file, not merely declared over an average
controls.knownLimit: Scoped to src/lib, src/store and src/config on purpose — the UI layer is covered by E2E, and e2e/COVERAGE.md is the compensating control for it. Within that scope the floor is now per-file with no glob exemptions: the aggregate form of this threshold hid five files below 80% behind a 91% total on 2026-09-15, customer/client.ts at 0% among them, which is what issue 14 of that review recorded and what perFile: true closed on 2026-09-18.

controls.claims: no workflow condition reads another step's result while silently also requiring that nothing earlier succeeded
one pnpm version resolves this lockfile, and the four CVE overrides cannot be removed without a test failing
controls.knownLimit: Covers this repository's declarations only. Dependabot resolves lockfiles on its own infrastructure and honours `packageManager`, but nothing here can prove it did — the evidence is that the regenerated lockfile still carries its `overrides:` block, which `--frozen-lockfile` checks on every run.

controls.claims: one declared Node version resolves this repository, and every workflow and Vercel read it from the same field
controls.knownLimit: Covers this repository's declarations only. Vercel reads `engines.node` from its own build image and nothing here can prove which patch it resolved — the guarantee is that it reads the same field, and the same major, as CI does. Playwright is deliberately outside this control: `ci.yml` derives the browser version from the installed `@playwright/test` package and keys its cache on it, so the lockfile is already that tool's single authority and a second declaration would be the regression.

controls.claims: package.json declares each key once, and its ranges agree with pnpm-lock.yaml, checked before the install that both files break
controls.knownLimit: Two questions, one of them newly answered and one newly *named*. Duplicate keys in package.json is the half nothing else asks: JSON permits them, JSON.parse takes the last occurrence silently, and on 2026-09-18 main carried five of them while every tool read one value from a file that stated two. Manifest/lockfile divergence is already detected by `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` — what this adds is that the failure arrives as a named red check with a package and two version strings, instead of as a dead install step that leaves every later check reporting `skipped` (ADR 011). It does **not** check pnpm-lock.yaml for duplicate keys: that needs a YAML parser, which is a dependency, and this runs before dependencies exist — pnpm already refuses such a lockfile outright. It reads the root importer only, so a workspace package would be outside it, and it compares declared ranges rather than resolved versions.

controls.claims: a pull request cannot raise the major of next, react, react-dom or any @shopify/* package without a written rationale in its description
controls.knownLimit: It reports; it does not block, because main has no branch protection and a red X sits beside a merge button anyone can still press. Registered as configured because the check itself runs and fails correctly — what is missing is the merge-gate control it would hang from, which is why that is its backstop rather than human:weekly. It also reads the package.json diff only: a major arriving through a transitive dependency, or through pnpm.overrides, is outside it. And `hasWrittenRationale` asks whether somebody wrote a paragraph under a heading, not whether the paragraph is any good — bounded coverage, stated rather than claimed (ADR 007). Until 2026-09-18 it read the description **frozen into the webhook payload** (`github.event.pull_request.body`), which made it unsatisfiable by the one action it demands: `pull_request` does not fire when a description is edited, and a re-run replays the original payload, so a `## Rationale` written in answer to this check's own failure message was invisible to it. The only sequence that cleared it was edit the description *then push a commit*. It now reads the body live from the pull requests API, so re-running the job is the remedy. What remains bounded is that nothing re-evaluates it automatically when the description changes — adding `pull_request: types: [edited]` would cancel the in-flight merge-gate run through ci.yml's ref-keyed concurrency group and replace it with a `skipped` indistinguishable from a pass, so the one click is the deliberate trade.
controls.humanAction: When this check fails and the rationale has since been written: re-run the `Dependency scope` job (Checks → Dependency scope → Re-run jobs). It reads the description live, so no commit on top is needed. If it still fails, the `## Rationale` heading is missing or the prose under it is under 40 characters — run `node scripts/audit-dependency-scope.mjs --base origin/main --json` to see exactly what it read and from where.

controls.claims: every consumer that installs from pnpm-lock.yaml passes --frozen-lockfile, so none of them can resolve around a lockfile the merge gate would reject
controls.knownLimit: Asserts what this repository declares, not what Vercel executes. A project-level Install Command set in the Vercel dashboard overrides vercel.json, and nothing here can read that — the same blind spot smoke-secret-isolation records for GitHub environment scoping. Verify it once in the dashboard and re-verify when the project is reconfigured; this check covers every other consumer, and covers the file a reviewer would read to answer the question.

controls.claims: a production-smoke failure repeating the same diagnosis escalates once instead of commenting every six hours, and the comparison that decides "same diagnosis" is a pure function with fixture tests rather than a string inside a YAML file
no github-script step in any workflow holds a decision: each is within a 45-line transport budget, and the four blocks that exceed it today are frozen at their current size and may not grow
every recorded decision that rests on a live premise has a detector that reports when the premise drifts
controls.knownLimit: Runs only inside production-smoke, whose real checks have not executed since 2026-08-15. A detector downstream of a failing preflight is a detector that is not running — which is what the smoke-liveness control exists to say out loud.

controls.claims: the tests protecting seventeen named invariants can still fail when those invariants are broken
controls.knownLimit: Covers seventeen declared sentinels, not the whole suite. A dead assertion outside that set is invisible to it, and the sentinel anchors are exact strings that a refactor will move — which is why the probe reports `unapplicable` loudly rather than skipping.

controls.claims: something has actually verified the live store within the last 26 hours
controls.knownLimit: Cannot detect its own death. If control-audit.yml stops running, nothing reports that — the honest end of any monitoring chain, recorded rather than closed with a fourth watcher (ADR 006's precedent). It is also blind to a run whose step data the Actions API will not return, which it reports as unevaluable rather than as dark.

controls.claims: if CI runs on main stop evaluating the repository, an issue says so — a run that dies in setup reports every check as skipped, which from outside is indistinguishable from success
controls.knownLimit: Keys on the `Lint` step alone. A run whose lint executed has evaluated the repository, so an ordinary red build reads as `lit` — deliberately, because demanding that every check ran would alarm on each genuinely broken pull request and become a muted channel (ADR 011). It follows that a gate broken *after* lint, between lint and build, is not covered here; the merge gate's own red X carries that.

controls.claims: the hero copy card may occupy no more than 60% of the photograph it sits on
every header control is reachable inside the viewport down to 320px
the product image tile is square, capped, and contained at every viewport
every route excused from E2E in e2e/COVERAGE.md names a test that exists and covers it
controls.knownLimit: Checks that a cited test exists and mentions the route, not that its assertions still mean anything — that is the fossil question, answered by control:assertion-liveness. Two of the nine exceptions were wrong the first time this ran: /api/version cited a file that tests the version-literal scan and never imports the route, leaving that route with no test at all, and /api/shopify cited an E2E spec that does not touch it.

controls.claims: every failure mode the code enumerates as a type is documented in docs/failure-modes.md with what detects it and what covers it
controls.knownLimit: Reconciles the seven registered union types in both directions; a failure mode with no type cannot be found by it. Those are listed in the document’s final table by hand, which is the part of the registry that can still go stale — a new un-enumerated degradation is invisible to this check in exactly the way an undocumented union member is not.

controls.claims: no two rate limiters share a Redis key prefix, so no two budgets silently merge
controls.knownLimit: Static by necessity, not by preference. With Upstash unconfigured — every test environment today — the in-memory fallback allocates a fresh Map per limiter and ignores the prefix entirely, so a collision is invisible to any test that drives requests through a route and appears only in production. A prefix built from a constant rather than written inline would also be missed, which is why the check asserts it found at least five limiters.

controls.claims: the unit suite runs under the same environment locally and in the merge gate, so a green local run is evidence about the gate
controls.knownLimit: Reconciles the declared environments, not the measured coverage. A module whose branch count depends on some *other* ambient difference — a locale, a TZ, a Node minor — is outside it. The real defence against that class is a test stubbing both arms, as config-env-branches.test.ts does for src/config; this control only removes the one difference that had already cost three red CI runs on 2026-09-18 while every local run was clean.

$decisionAdrsComment: Every ADR is classified: it either describes a control (and appears as an `adr` above) or
it records a decision (and appears here with the reason it is not a control).
There is no third option, because 'unclassified' is how --sage shipped as 9-13px text at
1.97:1 in four places, and how a gate nothing enforced was asserted by five documents.
A control, for this purpose, is a mechanism whose absence is not visible from the thing it
protects. A decision is reasoning that is wrong out loud when violated.

decisionAdrs.docs/adr/001-two-webhook-secrets.md: Records which of two secrets Shopify signs with. A fact about an external system, not a mechanism that can go missing.
decisionAdrs.docs/adr/002-cart-completion-discriminat: A code-level discriminator. Its absence is a failing test, not a silent one.
A module boundary. Violating it is a lint or type error at the point of violation.
decisionAdrs.docs/adr/004-static-fallback-is-not-a-da: An architectural rule. Its enforcement mechanism is the premise-detectors control above.
decisionAdrs.docs/adr/005-english-only-storefront.md: A scope decision, watched by the premise-detectors control rather than being one.
decisionAdrs.docs/adr/007-regex-guardrails-have-unkno: A rule about how controls are written, not a control. It constrains the entries above.
decisionAdrs.docs/adr/009-api-version-must-be-asserte: Asserted inside verify-production.mjs, which the premise-detectors and smoke-liveness controls already cover.
decisionAdrs.docs/adr/012-an-unassigned-escalation-is: An escalation convention for humans. Covered mechanically by the smoke-escalation control above.
A palette decision. Its enforcement is design-tokens-contrast.test.ts, which fails loudly in the gate.
decisionAdrs.docs/adr/018-a-claim-about-a-control-is-: The rule this registry implements. It is the frame, not an entry in it.
decisionAdrs.docs/adr/021-a-metric-with-only-one-dire: A rule about how sizes are written, and the audit that enforces it runs in the fast gate and fails by name. Its absence would be visible, which is what makes it a guardrail rather than a control.
decisionAdrs.docs/adr/019-an-unclassified-entry-is-an: A rule about how enumerations are written, like ADR 007 is about how guardrails are written. Its three reconciliation tests run in the fast gate and fail by name, so their absence would be visible; that is what makes them guardrails rather than controls.
decisionAdrs.docs/adr/023-the-last-link-is-a-person.m: States where the verification regress terminates. It is the frame the backstop field implements, not an entry in it — and its enforcement is a registry test that fails loudly in the fast gate.
decisionAdrs.docs/adr/024-a-tool-never-pointed-at-a-k: A rule about how verification tools are built and admitted to this registry. Like ADR 007, it constrains the entries rather than being one.
decisionAdrs.docs/adr/025-a-number-in-prose-is-a-clai: A rule about how documentation is written. Its reconciler runs in the fast gate and fails by name, so its absence would be visible — a guardrail, not a control.
decisionAdrs.docs/adr/028-a-fixture-is-the-input-you-: A rule about how verification tools are tested before being relied upon, like ADR 007 is about how guardrails are written and ADR 024 about pointing them at a known answer. It constrains the entries rather than being one, and its enforcement is parser-fuzz.test.ts, which fails by name in the fast gate.
decisionAdrs.docs/adr/026-a-capability-is-not-a-verdi: A rule about how a control decides whether it may run: gate on what a check needs, not on whether the whole setup is valid. Its enforcement is preflight-secrets.test.ts and the workflow's own conditions, which fail loudly in the fast gate.

$backstopComment: Every control names what catches ITS OWN failure, and following the chain must end at a person.
`control:<id>` points at another entry. `human:<cadence>` is the floor. There is no third form,
and a cycle is a failure: two controls backstopping each other is a chain with no bottom.
This exists because the bottom rung broke on arrival. control-audit.yml — the tier that watches
every other control — was invalid YAML from the commit that created it and produced three runs
with zero jobs. Nothing in this repository noticed. A human reading the Actions tab did.
ADR 022 conceded the audit cannot detect its own death and left it there. This says where the
regress stops instead: docs/weekly-verification.md, five minutes, once a week, regardless of what
any dashboard says — because the premise is that the dashboards may be lying.
$acceptedComment: A `not-configured` control names when its gap was accepted and why.
probe-branch-protection.mjs exits 0 while the registry honestly says not-configured, so an
accepted gap raises no alarm — correctly, since a six-hourly alarm about a state only a human can
change is the channel ADR 011 says people learn to mute.
But silence has its own failure: `accepted` decays into `forgotten`, and nothing marks the moment.
So the acceptance expires instead of the alarm firing. control-registry.test.ts fails when an
acceptance is older than ACCEPTED_GAP_MAX_AGE_DAYS, which forces a person to restate it or close
it — once, in a diff a reviewer sees, rather than every six hours in a channel nobody reads.
